claims.text: The target material family is multiphase Ni-based superalloys containing γ′ precipitates.
The primary mechanical property of interest is tensile ductility, measured as elongation to failure.
Aging at 0.6–0.7 Tm causes an initial decrease and subsequent recovery in ductility.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by γ′ interfaces evolving from coherent to semi-coherent to incoherent states.
Increasing precipitate size changes the dominant dislocation interaction from precipitate shearing to Orowan bypassing.
Small coherent γ′ precipitates are sheared by dislocations.
Shearing of coherent γ′ precipitates produces high work hardening but limited ductility through planar slip and localized deformation.
Precipitate growth causes loss of coherency and forces dislocations to bypass the precipitates through Orowan looping.
The shearing-to-bypassing transition causes a sharp ductility decrease because of interfacial stress concentration.
At long aging times, increased interparticle spacing and stable semi-coherent interfaces promote homogeneous dislocation distributions and cross-slip.
Homogeneous dislocation distribution and cross-slip at long aging times recover tensile ductility.
The ductility-versus-aging-time curve has a U or V shape, with its minimum at the critical precipitate size for the shearing-to-bypassing transition.
The non-monotonic transition occurs only at γ′ volume fractions of 15–30%.
The transition requires aging temperatures at which coherency loss and precipitate growth kinetically separate the shearing and bypassing regimes.
The transition is absent at very low precipitate volume fractions and when precipitates are incoherent from the outset.
Re or Ru additions can alter stacking-fault energy and interfacial energy and thereby shift the critical precipitate size.
The initial solution-treated and quenched Ni-10Al-10Ti-5Cr-2Mo alloy is a supersaturated solid solution with a high density of γ′ nucleation sites.
The proposed intervention is isothermal aging at 750 °C for durations from 1 to 1000 hours.
Standard aging produces a monotonic ductility decrease through precipitate coarsening and loss of matrix strength.
Monotonic ductility loss, or failure of the ductility minimum to coincide with the observed shearing-to-bypassing transition, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis presents aging as a coherent-to-semi-coherent-to-incoherent progression, whereas the mechanism attributes the long-time recovery to formation of a stable semi-coherent interface after precipitates have already grown and lost coherency. The long-time interfacial state is therefore internally inconsistent.
